Subject: Unexpected throughput collapse overnight — immediate support needed

Logan / Redwood team,

We woke up this morning to a sustained 10-15% increase in token queueing and a doubling of 5xx errors on our reserved capacity routes between 02:00–04:30 PDT. This is hitting transaction processing for several merchants. Our dashboards show reserved throughput utilization pegged and a lot of tail latency.

I attached a short sample of API errors and a CSV of per-route reservation utilization from the early-morning window. We’re seeing a mix of 429/503 and some 500s with "kv-cache-miss" traces. Can someone confirm whether this was a planned maintenance or unexpected saturation? We need an ETA on mitigation and whether you can authorize burst capacity for today.

Attachments: error-sample-logs.txt, reserved-utilization.csv

—Sara
Sara Levine

Team — quick triage notes from ops (on-call):

- Root symptom: dedicated GPU pool serving NimblePay routes hit sustained headroom depletion across two racks between 02:10–04:20 PDT. Kernel-level queuing increased and preemption queued requests while KV cache thrash spiked.
- Reserved capacity: utilization report indicates NimblePay’s reserved pool was at 98–101% (burst credits already consumed earlier this week).
- Error pattern: majority 429s from request throttling and ~6% 5xx (OOM guardrail fallbacks and a small cluster of 503s where fallback to smaller model failed). See attached slo-metrics-10-01.png for latency distribution.

Immediate mitigations we can execute now (requires decision):
1) Canary model swap: route a small percentage to a quantized variant (reduces per-token GPU time) — low risk, needs config push (~15m).
2) Emergency burst: allocate on-demand dedicated capacity for ~2 hours — we need exec authorization for burst spend and ops to grant placement (30–45m).
3) Auto-fallback policy: enable model-level fallback to a cheaper variant for non-critical endpoints — config-only, low risk, immediate.

Recommendation: enable (1) and (3) immediately; request (2) if (1)+(3) don’t reduce queueing within 30 minutes. If exec approves burst, we will run it with a routing policy that isolates NimblePay traffic to new racks to avoid noisy-neighbor spill.
